title: World records

fn.en: Talk about the most extreme things in the world and in your own life.

useful: It’s the biggest in the world.

items.a: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world
Kilimanjaro is one of the largest volcanoes
Beijing is the busiest airport of the three
The Great Pyramid is the oldest in this group

items.q: From the top of the water to the bottom. The lake is 1,600 metres…
From the bottom of the mountain to the top. It is 5,895 metres…
From one side of the river to the other. It is 400 metres…
Ninety million passengers a year. It is the ___ airport.
Everybody goes there in the summer. It is very ___.
A town on an oil platform in the sea is very ___.

tts: We say the in superlatives with a weak sound when the following adjective starts with a consonant. We say the ending -est with a schwa sound.
the biggest lake — the deepest lake — the oldest lake

sub.en: Look at the sentences. What comes before the superlative — and what after it?

items.q: Lake Baikal is ___ lake in the world.
items.why: A superlative almost always takes the: the deepest, the most expensive.

items.q: Tokyo is ___ city in this list.
Beijing is ___ airport of the three.
items.why: consonant + y → -iest: busy → busiest, easy → easiest.

items.q: August is ___ month of the year here.

items.why: good → the best, bad → the worst.

items.q: Kilimanjaro is one of ___ volcanoes in the world.
items.why: “one of the …-est” is always plural after it: one of the largest volcanoes.

items.q: It’s the deepest lake ___ the world.
It’s the busiest airport ___ the three.

items.from: Baikal is deeper than every other lake.
items.a: Baikal is the deepest lake in the world

items.from: Beijing is busier than the other two airports.
items.a: Beijing is the busiest airport of the three

items.from: Tokyo is more expensive than the other cities.
items.a: Tokyo is the most expensive city

items.from: Kilimanjaro is a very large volcano.
items.a: Kilimanjaro is one of the largest volcanoes

items.from: August is hotter than every other month.
This photo is better than all my others.
items.a: This is the best photo I have

acts.title: Four records and one town
text: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the biggest, deepest and oldest lake in the world. It is more than 1,600 metres deep and more than twenty-five million years old, and it holds almost twenty per cent of all the fresh water on the planet.
Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is one of the largest volcanoes in the world and, at 5,895 metres, the highest mountain in Africa.
Beijing has the busiest airport of the three biggest in the world; Dubai is second and Los Angeles third. Greenland is the biggest island, and Madagascar is bigger than Sumatra.

The strangest place on this list is not a record at all. Neft Dashlari is a town built on an oil platform in the Caspian Sea: three hundred kilometres of streets, two thousand people, a cinema and a park — and no land under any of it.

items.s: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.
Lake Baikal is about one million years old.
Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa.
Los Angeles has the busiest airport of the three.
Neft Dashlari is built on land.

write.q: Write your own six records: three about the world and three about your own life (the longest journey you made, the best meal you ate, the most unusual place you visited). Use at least four superlatives and one “one of the …”.
write.ph: The deepest lake in the world is…
write.model: The deepest lake in the world is Baikal — more than 1,600 metres deep. Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa. Beijing has the busiest airport of the three. In my own life, the longest journey I made was thirty hours by train to Georgia. The best meal I ate was in a small village near Tbilisi. Almaty is one of the most beautiful cities I know.

speak.q: Answer out loud: What’s the highest mountain in your country? What’s the longest journey you made? What’s the most unusual place you visited?
speak.model: The highest mountain in Kazakhstan is Khan Tengri, almost seven thousand metres. The longest journey I made was thirty hours by train. The most unusual place I visited was a town built on the water.
